why: MenuItem takes props and reads props.name and props.price instead of destructuring { name, price }. It renders the same three lines (Tacos: $9, Burrito: $11, Churros: $5); the plan's pass line is that MenuItem reads name and price props and is rendered three times, which holds. Destructuring is style, not the skill.

step.title: Read name and price in MenuItem
step.instructions:
In src/MenuItem.jsx, write a MenuItem component that takes name and price props (destructure them in the parameter list) and returns
  • {name}: ${price}
    • . In src/Menu.jsx, render three MenuItems with a name and a price each.

targets.caption: Take name and price as props

checks.label: MenuItem shows the name and price

hints: Props arrive as one object; { name, price } in the parameter list pulls the two out.
common_mistakes: Writing function MenuItem(name, price): the first argument is the whole props object.
